title: A proof run is only at one full commit whose tree has no uncommitted change
when: RecordProofRun runs with a clean tree at the full commit, and then with a short commit, a branch, an upper-case commit, a tree at another commit, a changed file and an untracked file. Then ReadCheckout reads git repositories in which git status, as the repository and the user configure it, shows no change: a clean one, and ones with a change hidden by skip-worktree, a spec change hidden by assume-unchanged, an untracked file hidden by info/exclude, an untracked file hidden by the user's excludes file, another commit's tree shown by a replace ref, a same-size change hidden by minimal stat checks, and a new file hidden by an untracked .gitignore that ignores itself. ReadCommittedSpec reads the spec at the commit of the repositories whose spec change is hidden or replaced.
then: The clean runs give a proof run at the commit. atOneCleanCommit refuses each other run, and the store gets nothing. The spec read at the commit does not hold the hidden or replaced test record.

title: Every automated test record has an outcome, and a test that did not run is failed with did not run
when: With a spec of three automated test records and one that is not automated yet: RecordProofRun reads output in which only one automated test ran, and it was skipped.
then: The proof run holds the three automated test records in ID order: the skipped one as skipped, and the two others as failed with the detail did not run. The record that is not automated yet has no outcome.

title: A proof run with an outcome for an unknown ID is refused and names each such ID
when: RecordProofRun reads output with two IDs that are not test records, and then output with the ID of a test record that is not automated yet.
then: outcomesNameKnownRecords refuses the first run and names both IDs in order, and the store gets nothing. The second run is accepted with that outcome.

title: A proof run is attested only by the provider's trusted signer with its commit as subject
when: RecordProofRun runs in the trusted workflow at main, and then in another workflow. attestedByTrustedSigner checks the trusted workflow at main, and attestations with another commit, predicate type, workflow, repository or issuer.
then: The proof run's attestation names the commit, the proof run predicate type and the trusted signer, and the trusted workflow at main is accepted. Each other attestation is refused, and the run in another workflow is refused with nothing given to the store.

title: A proof run is never written as a file in the product's repository
when: GitHubAttestations hands over a proof run to a file at the repository's root, in a folder of the repository, through a path that climbs back in, through a link to a folder or a file in the repository, and through a relative path from inside it.
then: outsideTheRepository refuses each, and the repository keeps its files as they were. A file in a folder outside the repository is accepted.

title: A test record gets one outcome: failed if any run failed, else skipped if any was skipped, else passed
when: RecordProofRun reads Go and Python output in which each test record ID runs two or three times: passed, failed and passed; passed, skipped and passed; skipped and failed; passed twice.
then: Each test record has one outcome: failed, skipped, failed and passed.

title: A change decision names the change's commit, the base head and both coverages, and a release decision names only its commit
when: namesBothCommits checks a change decision with both commits and both coverages and a release decision with only its commit; then change decisions with no base head, a short one, a branch, no base coverage or a short commit, release decisions with a base head or a base coverage, and a decision of no gate kind.
then: The first two are accepted, and the change decision's text names both commits and both coverages. Each other decision is refused by namesBothCommits.

title: A refused decision names every obligation that fell and every test record that did not pass, and a passed decision names no reason
when: namesEveryCause checks, against two obligations that fell and two test records that did not pass, a refusal that names all four and a passed decision with no reason; then a refusal that leaves out an obligation, one that leaves out a test record, a refusal with no reason, and a passed decision with reasons.
then: The first two are accepted, and the refusal's text lists each cause on a line of its own. Each other decision is refused by namesEveryCause, which names the cause left out.

title: A passed release decision is handed to the attestation action about its commit, for the trusted signer at main, and nothing else is
when: With a fixture repository whose release commit is fully proved and a passed proof run signed at main: assure gate release runs as the gate-release job of the trusted workflow at main; then as a job of the trusted workflow at a pull request's ref and as a job of another workflow; then with a failed test; then with a predicate file inside the repository, and with a step summary inside the repository; then, for a passed and for a refused release, with an earlier file already at the predicate's path; then, with a step summary file set, at a commit whose spec has a test record of an invariant that does not exist, and for the passed release with the predicate's folder read-only. Then it runs with a step summary file set and no --predicate. Reads the attest-release job of proof-run.yml and runs its subject step for the commit.
then: The first run passes, its decision names the attestation at the release-decision predicate type about the commit, for the proof-run workflow at main, and it writes a predicate that is a passed release decision about the commit. releaseAttested refuses the passed decision in the two other jobs: each exits 2 with no decision and writes no predicate. The refused decision names no attestation and writes no predicate. With the predicate or the step summary inside the repository, and with an earlier file at the predicate's path, the gate exits 2 before it decides, prints no decision, writes no predicate and leaves the earlier file as it was; the repository has no change. At the commit with the broken spec the gate exits 2 and the step summary holds only one line that says no decision was reached. With the read-only folder the gate exits 2, writes no predicate, and the step summary holds the passed decision and then one line that says no decision was reached because the predicate is not written; this part is not checked when the tests run as root. With no --predicate it exits 2, and the step summary holds one line that says no decision was reached because the gate is called wrongly. The attest-release job is exactly its allowed keys and steps, and signs the predicate at the release-decision predicate type, with the commit as the subject that its subject step names.

title: The same causes give the same reasons in the same fixed order, and reasons out of that order are refused
when: The causes of a refusal, obligations that fell from shares, are absent at the change or lack a share at a release commit, no verified proof run, test records not passed, code-standard faults and workflow files that differ, are given in three orders, one with causes twice, and each gives a decision; then reasonsInFixedOrder checks reasons with a test record before an obligation, a workflow file before a test record, built before designed, obligations out of order, an absent obligation before another, proved before built at a release, a share not had before an obligation, the missing proof run after a test record, test records or workflow files out of order, a code fault before a test record, before an obligation or before the missing proof run, a workflow file before a code fault, code faults out of rule order or of one rule out of key order, and a reason or a code fault twice.
then: Each order gives the same reasons in the fixed order, each once: obligations, the proof run and test records, code faults by rule and key, then workflow files; and the same decision text, byte for byte. Each list out of the fixed order is refused by reasonsInFixedOrder.

title: A failed or interrupted resolution leaves go.mod and go.sum as they were, or recoverable to the resolved pair
when: With a project with applied code, go.mod and go.sum, and a fake go runner: Resolution fails in nine ways (the tidy, verify, list and diff commands; a source file added, edited or deleted during the run; go.mod edited during the run; and cancellation), and is interrupted at four points of the apply journal (before it is written, when it is written, after its first operation, and before it is complete).
then: Each failed run keeps the bytes of go.mod and go.sum and leaves no journal. An interruption before the journal is written keeps the old pair; each later interruption asks for recovery, and recovery writes exactly the resolved pair and removes the journal.

title: A saved overlay flag and ambient GOFLAGS cannot change what resolution reads
when: A project module replaces example.com/overlay with a local folder, and a saved Go configuration names an overlay that would make the project source import it; GOFLAGS in the environment holds an invalid flag. Resolution runs the module tools on the staged go.mod.
then: The overlay's import never reaches go.mod, and the source is unchanged.
notes: It covers the example the invariant names, a saved -overlay flag, plus ambient GOFLAGS and a GOWORK that points nowhere (ST-BLD-UC01-R02-T02). A real go.work or -modfile is not exercised.

title: A cache holds only module zips whose hashes go.sum states, and its record lists each
when: With a download cache of two module zips, one with an escaped path, and the hashes go.sum states for them: the cache is checked; then go.sum loses one hash; then it states a different hash for one zip; and cache records with no modules, a bad hash, a wrong order, a repeated module or an invalid path are checked.
then: The first check lists both modules by path, version and hash in order, and the record that lists them is valid. The zip that go.sum does not state is refused by name, the zip whose hash differs is refused with both hashes, and each changed record is refused.

title: A build runs with the proxy off from its recorded cache, and fails when a module is missing or differs
when: With a real build from a downloaded module cache: its record is read; then builds run from copies of the cache in which the module zip is missing, and in which it is changed.
then: The record names the module proxy off and the cache's inventory, and its environment sets GOPROXY off. Each build from a broken copy fails.
notes: It runs on the real build in TestBuildIsReproducibleAndRecordsEveryInput, so it needs the Go SDK that STEGO pins: STEGO_TEST_PINNED_GO names its bin/go, else the SDK that runs the test is used, and the test skips when STEGO refuses that SDK as not the pinned one. A skip is not a pass. It is local (ST-STD-LOCAL-R03): the download runs in process against the local module proxy and sum database of proxytest (ST-BLD-TOOL10), which play proxy.golang.org and sum.golang.org with a key made for each run; the records still name proxy.golang.org. ST-BLD-UC02-R01-T03 runs the stego binary against proxy.golang.org as a second, external proof. The download and both builds of TestBuildIsReproducibleAndRecordsEveryInput run in process (runBuild); stego build verify runs through the binary.

title: A build refuses an SDK that is not the verified one
when: With build options naming a fake go binary: Build runs.
then: It refuses the SDK and writes no work directory.
notes: Not proof yet: the pin is the compiler's sdkIdentity constant, not the archetype's; the archetype pin is not built (ST-SUP-INV08). Accepting the right SDK needs the real SDK.

title: Two builds from the same inputs give byte-identical executables, records and SBOMs
when: With a committed project, its downloaded module cache and the pinned Go SDK: stego build runs twice into new folders, each build building twice inside.
then: The two results hold byte-identical executables, build records, SPDX SBOMs and CycloneDX SBOMs.
notes: It runs on the real build in TestBuildIsReproducibleAndRecordsEveryInput, so it needs the Go SDK that STEGO pins: STEGO_TEST_PINNED_GO names its bin/go, else the SDK that runs the test is used, and the test skips when STEGO refuses that SDK as not the pinned one. A skip is not a pass. It is local (ST-STD-LOCAL-R03): the download runs in process against the local module proxy and sum database of proxytest (ST-BLD-TOOL10), which play proxy.golang.org and sum.golang.org with a key made for each run; the records still name proxy.golang.org. ST-BLD-UC02-R01-T03 runs the stego binary against proxy.golang.org as a second, external proof. The download and both builds of TestBuildIsReproducibleAndRecordsEveryInput run in process (runBuild); stego build verify runs through the binary.

title: The record of a real build names every input and the fixed build settings, and no credential
when: With a committed project that the compiler applied, whose generated program needs one small module, its downloaded module cache, the pinned Go SDK, and a credential and GOFLAGS in the caller's environment: stego build runs from the cache.
then: build.json names the revision, the Go SDK, the module cache inventory, the generation record, both builds, the executable's digest and the digest of every committed file; it sets CGO off, no workspace, the local toolchain, no GOFLAGS, the proxy off, telemetry off, read-only modules, trimmed paths, no PGO and no source stamping; it holds neither the credential, the caller's GOFLAGS, PATH nor HOME.
notes: It needs the Go SDK that STEGO pins: STEGO_TEST_PINNED_GO names its bin/go, else the SDK that runs the test is used, and the test skips when STEGO refuses that SDK as not the pinned one. A skip is not a pass. It builds a small program twice in each of two builds, about a minute. It is local (ST-STD-LOCAL-R03): the download runs in process against the local module proxy and sum database of proxytest (ST-BLD-TOOL10), which play proxy.golang.org and sum.golang.org with a key made for each run; the records still name proxy.golang.org. ST-BLD-UC02-R01-T03 runs the stego binary against proxy.golang.org as a second, external proof. The download and both builds of TestBuildIsReproducibleAndRecordsEveryInput run in process (runBuild); stego build verify runs through the binary.

title: An image build refuses an untrusted build record, CA bundle or executable and never reads the host's trust store
when: With a build record, its executable and an explicit CA bundle on disk, and SSL_CERT_FILE and SSL_CERT_DIR set to another CA: BuildImage runs with an untrusted build record digest, an untrusted CA digest, the host's CA bundle, a leaf certificate bundle, no CA bundle, an executable the record does not name, and an executable that is not the built one; then an image is assembled from the explicit CA bundle.
then: Each build is refused and writes no image.json; the assembled image holds the explicit CA bundle only, and an empty, private key or leaf certificate bundle is refused.
notes: TestTrustStoreRejectsKeysAndNonCACertificates in the same file also carries this ID and covers each malformed CA bundle. The accepted build needs a real Go executable that Verify accepts, so the success path is shown through assembleImage.

title: An image signature holds both SBOMs of its build record as signed attestations
when: With an image folder as image build writes it, with both SBOMs, and a provider verifier that gives an SPDX and a CycloneDX attestation about the image digest by the trusted signer: SignImage runs; then with the CycloneDX attestation of another predicate type, the SPDX attestation twice, a changed SPDX predicate, a changed CycloneDX file, an unsigned CycloneDX bundle, and a removed SPDX file.
then: The first run writes signature.json with both attestations in the order SPDX, CycloneDX and the digest of each SBOM, and a second run does not replace it; each change is refused and writes no signature.json.

title: A signature by any identity other than the pipeline's trusted signer is refused
when: With a trusted keyless signer: the signer check runs on another workflow, another reference, another issuer, a key and keyless identity, no identity, a key, and a subject with no exact reference; on trusted signers that are both, neither, without an exact reference, on plain HTTP or with a short key digest; and SignImage runs on an image whose SBOM attestations are by another workflow.
then: Each other identity and each invalid trusted signer is refused, and SignImage refuses the image, names the trusted signer and writes no signature.json.
notes: Which signer a provider has comes from the service's delivery pipeline (ST-DLV-INV04); here the trusted signer is an input of the test.

title: The same build gives the same image, running as non-root
when: With one executable and one CA bundle: The image is assembled twice, in two different directories.
then: Both records are equal and both OCI layouts have the same digests; the config runs as user 65532, with entrypoint /service and SSL_CERT_FILE set.
notes: It calls assembleImage, the whole of what stego image build writes after its checks.

title: The source snapshot is the Git tree of the revision
when: With a revision whose export attributes, links and malformed entries would change the extracted tree: capture the source snapshot.
then: Each extracted file matches the raw Git object, and each link, special file and attribute-changed input is refused.
notes: Proved by TestSourceArchiveMustMatchRawGitObjects once its name or a subtest carries this ID. TestGitExportAttributesCannotChangeSelectedSource and TestSourceTreeRejectsLinksAndMalformedEntries in the same file cover the refusals.

title: Image verification is exact
when: With an image whose hashes are rebuilt to be consistent after one change: it runs as root, has an ambient environment value, a writable executable, a symbolic link, an extra executable, a private key in its trust store, a device, another owner, or unknown PAX metadata; verify it.
then: Each variant is refused and named.
notes: TestImageRejectsChangedLayoutAndRecord in the same file covers an extra layout file, a link, changed bytes and a missing blob. An excessive size is refused by the layer limit, which no test exercises.

title: Registry transport is bounded and fails closed
when: With a registry that answers over plain HTTP, demands a token from an unapproved origin, redirects with a query string or sends an oversized response: publish and retrieve.
then: Each case fails closed before any credential leaves, and the error names no credential.
notes: TestRegistryTLSCredentialsAndPolicyFailClosed carries this ID. TestRegistryBearerRealmNeedsExplicitApproval, TestRegistryTokenScopeCannotExpandCredentials, TestRegistryResponseAndRequestBounds and TestRegistryBoundaryRejectsCredentialLeaksAndPathEscapes in the same file cover the token origins, the bounds and the errors.

title: A build starts in new folders outside the source, and a failed save leaves no result
when: With a source, a module cache and a folder an interrupted build left: a build is prepared with new folders, then with the interrupted folder as its work or result folder, and with a work or result folder inside the source or a result folder inside the work folder; then the result is saved without an executable and with an executable that differs from the record.
then: Only the new folders are accepted; the source and the interrupted folder keep their files; each failed save removes the result folder it made.
notes: This proves Build's part (appbuild.prepare and appbuild.saveResult in build.go). The image build's part is in internal/appbuild/image.go, which keeps a partial output folder when it fails; the SDK preparation's part is test_existing_output_is_never_removed_or_replaced in scripts/test_compiler_toolchain.py.

title: A declaration without exactly one archetype is refused
when: Checking reads a declaration with no archetype; with two archetypes, test-arch and other-arch, given as a list; with the archetype nonexistent-arch, which the registry does not hold; and with the one archetype test-arch.
then: Expects the first three declarations to be refused with an archetype fault: the first names the archetype as missing, the second names both archetypes, and the third names nonexistent-arch. Expects the last declaration to be accepted.
notes: Proved by TestValidate_MissingArchetype, subtest ST-DECL-INV01-T: no archetype, two archetypes and an unknown archetype are each refused with a fault that names the archetype field (and both names, or the unknown name); one archetype is accepted.

title: A declaration that carries an undeclared field is refused
when: With a declaration that carries a misspelled field at the root, in an entity field, in a collection or in a slot binding: parse it.
then: The parser refuses the declaration with an error that names the unknown field, the file and the line.

title: A declaration must be one document with no anchors, aliases or merge keys
when: With a declaration that holds a second document, an empty second document, an anchor or a merge key: parse it.
then: The parser refuses the declaration with an error that names the fault, the file and the line.

title: A declaration beyond 4 MiB or 128 levels is refused
when: Decode a declaration one byte over 4 MiB, decode a declaration nested 130 levels deep, and parse a file one byte over 4 MiB.
then: Each is refused, and the errors name the nesting limit and the byte limit.

title: A repeated entity name is refused
when: With a declaration that defines the same entity name twice: validate it.
then: The check reports an entity fault that says the entity is defined more than once.

title: A repeated field name in one entity is refused
when: With a declaration whose entity has two fields with the same name: validate it.
then: The check reports a field fault that names the entity and the repeated field name.

title: A field's constraints must suit its type
when: With a declaration whose fields carry constraints that do not suit their types, such as a length limit on a number, a numeric bound on a string, a pattern on a boolean, enum values on a string and a reference target on a string: validate it; and client_set on a string, on created_at and updated_at, on a computed timestamp, and on the timestamp due_at.
then: The check reports one field fault for each unsuitable constraint, and each fault names the constraint and the field type. client_set is refused on the string, on created_at and updated_at and on the computed timestamp, each fault naming the field and the reason, and accepted on due_at (ST-DECL-Q16).

title: A repeated collection name is refused
when: With a declaration that defines the same collection name twice: validate it.
then: The check refuses the declaration with one reading fault that names the repeated name widgets and the line of its second definition (service.yaml:16).
notes: Collections are a map in the declaration format, so a repeated collection name is a repeated key and the declaration cannot be read as one document. ST-DECL-UC04-R06 then holds: the refusal is the one reading fault. This is not the stop at the first fault that ST-DECL-UC03-R02 forbids, so the test does not assert that validation stops.

title: A collection that names an undeclared entity is refused
when: With a declaration whose collection names an entity the declaration does not define: validate it.
then: The check reports a collection fault that names the missing entity.

title: A writable setting outside its values or that disagrees with the collections is refused with its path
when: Checking reads ST-DECL-TD02 with the collection todos given patch, with one change each: a field with writable sometimes; a field with writable Create; a computed field with writable create; a timestamp that is not client_set with writable never; a required enum field with writable never and no default; a field with writable create in the patchable list; and a field with writable never and a default first in the patchable list. Then a computed field with writable never and no default that the patchable list names. Then TD02 with a create field, a never field with a default, an optional never field with no default, a client-set timestamp with writable create and a field with writable always, and TD02 with a patchable field with writable always.
then: Expects one writable fault for each change, at the path of the setting or of the patchable entry, with the value found, the three allowed values for a value that is not one of them, and a message that names the field and the rule; one fault only, at the setting, for the computed never field that a patch names; and no writable fault for the declarations that keep the rule.
notes: The test calls checking in process on the declaration as a value. Mutations caught: no call of validateWritable from Validate; no refusal of a required never field with no default.

title: A secret field that is not a string, or that is a key, an index or a default, is refused
when: Checking reads the declaration of ST-DECL-TD02 with a secret field of Todo that is an int32, a bytes, a compare-only jsonb, unique, unique when live, with a unique_composite, in the unique_composite of another field, computed, with a default, compare_only on a public field, renamed and retyped by a schema change, given a fill value by a require, and in a declared invariant of kind unique; then with an implicit value of a secret field; then a readable and a compare-only secret string and a readable secret jsonb.
then: Expects each refused with the rule secret-field, a fault that names the field and ST-DECL-INV101 and never the default or the implicit value, and the last accepted.
notes: The test calls checking directly.

title: A seal of a readable secret is accepted, and a seal of another field, from another sensitivity or beside another change of the field is refused
when: Checking reads ST-DECL-TD02 with Todo.title secret and a seal of it from pii, public, secret and none at expand, and at contract; then a secret note with an add, a relax and a seal in this order; then a seal of a pii field, of a compare-only secret, of a field that Todo does not declare, from confidential, with a definition, two seals of title, and a seal before a relax of title; then a seal at expand with the modes api.
then: Expects the first six accepted; each other refused with a fault that names the change and its reason, the bad From with ST-DECL-INV102 and the relax after the seal as only an add or a relax before the seal; and the last refused for the mode controller.
notes: The test calls checking directly. Walkthrough 13, W13-B1 for the From secret.

title: Checking refuses a relation service of the type tenant with no provisioning or with another subject type
when: Checking reads ST-DECL-TD03 with a definition tenant that declares the relation service: service; then one that declares only auditor: user; then the relation service: service with no tenant provisioning; then service: user; then service: service | user; then service: service:*; then service: service#operator; then service: service with ip_allowed; then service: service with expiration; then service: service | service:*.
then: Expects the first two to be accepted, and each of the others to be refused with one tenant-provisioning fault, found tenant#service, at tenancy.provisioning or tenancy.provisioning.resource_type, that names what is wrong.
notes: The test calls checking in process, as ST-DECL-INV95-T does. Each case is its own subtest, with this ID in its name. Walkthrough 13, W13-B4; ST-SUP-Q183 (a). The wildcard, relation, caveat and expiration cases: security review of PR 448, L1.

title: A limit of wrong attempts on a compare-only secret, its window and its reset are accepted, each other is refused, and a short window on a short secret is warned of
when: Checking reads ST-DECL-TD02 with Todo.pin, a compare-only secret, with the limits 1, 5 and 100 and the unlock_after 1m, 15m, 90s and 24h; then with the limit 0 and 101, with attempts on a readable secret, on a public field and on a pii field, and with the unlock_after 59s, 25h, 90.5s and soon. Then with Todo of the resource type todo, a counted pin and a compare-only code with no limit, and the command unlock-pin on a row of Todo with the permission unlock_pin and resets_attempts [Todo.pin]; then with resets_attempts of Todo.code, of Todo.colour, of Todo alone and of Todo.pin twice, with no permission, with no resource member, with the permission edit of the operations of Todo, and with the permission unlock_pin of another command withdraw. Then the warnings of a window of 15m on a PIN of min_length 4, of 23h on a secret with no min_length, of 24h, of no window, and of 15m on a secret of min_length 7. Then, with ST-DECL-TD03, a counted pin on Todo, the command withdraw with the permission operate and the command unlock-pin with resets_attempts [Todo.pin], and a schema whose document has operate = parent->viewer and whose folder has see = viewer and help = helper: unlock_pin = support, parent->help and alias = support; then owner + support, edit + support, parent->viewer, viewer, alias = parent->viewer, alias2 = owner and parent->see; and unlock_pin = support with operate = parent->viewer + unlock_pin. Then, with ST-DECL-TD03 and the command unlock-pin with the permission unlock_pin = support on document, beside the command pay on folder that writes Todo with the permission pay: with pay = parent->viewer on document, with no pay on document, and with pay = support on document; beside the command create-todo on the service-level resource that writes Todo; and, with no schema, beside the command pay on folder with the permission unlock_pin.
then: Expects the limits, the windows and the reset of the first command accepted, and each other case refused: a limit or a window with a fault of attempts-limit that names pin and ST-DECL-INV104, and a reset with a fault of resets-attempts that names unlock-pin, ST-DECL-INV104 and the cause. Expects one warning of attempts-guessable that names pin and ST-DECL-INV104 for the first two windows and none for the others; the first three accepted, and each other expression refused with one fault of resets-attempts that names the shared relation, permission or arrow, unlock-pin and ST-DECL-INV104. Expects the reset beside pay = parent->viewer and beside create-todo accepted, and each other case refused with one fault of resets-attempts that names unlock-pin, ST-DECL-INV104 and the command pay or the shared relation document#support.
notes: The test calls checking directly. Each case is its own subtest, with this ID in its name. Mutations caught (fu/standing-39): no bound of unlock_after; no check of a shared permission. Decision ST-SUP-Q185 (a); security review of PR #451, H1; decision ST-SUP-Q205 (c). Mutations caught (fu/standing-39, round 2): no check of the schema (the four expressions pass); no warning. Decision ST-SUP-Q207 (a); security review of PR #489, M2. Mutations caught (round 3, second review of PR #489, M2b): the check of the top-level arms only (the aliases, the reverse name and the arrow into folder pass). Mutations caught (fu/standing-40, decision ST-SUP-Q209 (d)): no commands of another resource type (resetWriters gives none); no check that the schema defines their permission on the resource type of the entity.

title: Event fields that are declared and public, or pii with a reason, are accepted, and each other list of event fields is refused
when: Checking reads ST-DECL-TD02 with the mixins durable-events and kafka-events and Todo with the fields title, done, email (pii) and token (secret), and Events of title and done; then of title and email with a reason for email; then with no field, 65 fields, a field that Todo does not declare, title twice, token, email with no reason, a reason for title, the version 0; and then Events of title in a declaration with no mixin that publishes change events.
then: Expects the first two accepted, and each other refused with a fault that names Todo, the field and ST-DECL-INV105.
notes: The test calls checking directly. Each case is its own subtest, with this ID in its name. Decision ST-SUP-Q184 (c).

title: A default, computed or filled_by on a scope field is refused
when: Checking reads a collection scoped by org_id whose entity gives org_id the default org-1, then the same collection with no default on org_id. Then checking reads a collection team-projects scoped by org_id and team_id, first with the default team-1 on team_id only, then with the default org-1 on org_id too. Then it reads the collection with org_id computed and filled_by org-filler; with org_id computed only; with org_id filled_by org-filler only; with the default org-1, computed and filled_by on org_id; and with no property on org_id, while the entity holds another computed field.

title: The architecture view is the same with or without hand-written notes, network or home folder
when: With a project in a temporary folder: the view is derived once; then once more with a README.md and a docs/architecture.md that describe other components, with no network, and with HOME set to an empty folder.
then: Expects the two views and the two model files to have the same bytes, and every element of the model to name a source in the declaration, the registry parts or the wiring of the run.
notes: A guessed element is ST-GEN-UC08-R05's refusal; this test shows that no outside input reaches the view.

title: Every run that writes code, apply and recover, writes the view and the model file, and the record holds their hashes
when: With an applied project in a temporary folder: the declaration gets an entity, and apply runs; then apply runs again with no change; then one byte of the view is changed and drift runs; then the view is restored, the declaration gets a second entity, apply stops after its journal is written, and recovery runs.
then: Expects the first apply to plan, write and record the view and the model file with the code, with their hashes in the record. Expects the second apply to change nothing. Expects drift to name the view. Expects the recovery to leave the view and the model file of the second entity's run, with their hashes in the new record, and drift then to report no change.
notes: Recover also writes generated code (ST-GEN-CMD02), so a run that writes the view only on apply fails the last case. It needs the hook that stops apply at a named journal point.

title: The generated module file requires the runtime library at the archetype's pin only, and a hand edit of it is drift
when: For each archetype of the registry: a project is applied, and the test reads its generated go.mod and go.sum; then go.mod gets in turn a pseudo-version of the runtime library, a replace directive for it, and a requirement of a second STEGO module, and drift runs after each.
then: Expects go.mod to require the runtime library at exactly the version that the archetype pins and go.sum to hold the pinned checksum, with no other module under STEGO's module path and no replace directive for one. Expects drift to name go.mod after each of the three edits.
notes: Proved by TestArchetypeRuntimePin; its subtest carries this ID. The test registries have one archetype each, at two versions with two different pins, and their one component emits a Go file that imports a package of the runtime library: go.mod requires the pin only when generated code imports it (decision of 2026-11-10 under the Product owner's delegation, ST-GEN-Q03 (a)). Drift reads go.mod against the pin that the record holds; a fourth edit, another tagged version, is drift too. Mutation check: the test fails when a check of runtimeModuleDrift, mergeRuntimeSum or the pin in moduleRequirements is taken out.

title: A generated service reads no declaration, scans nothing and registers nothing by name, tag or init
when: With ST-DECL-TD03 on the runtime data path and its three modes api, worker and controller stated, which a service on the runtime data path needs (ST-DECL-INV89) (rest-crud with tenancy, authorization, the command and query components and the postgres-adapter): stego apply runs on a project in a temporary folder, the test reads every generated Go file with go/ast, stego apply runs again, and the service is built with the pinned Go into one binary.
then: Expects no func init, no import of plugin, no string that names service.yaml, no go:embed of a YAML file, no call of os.Executable or debug.ReadBuildInfo, and no read of a struct tag in any generated Go file. The one allowed func init is the one that protoc-gen-go emits: in a file with the protoc-gen-go header, it only calls file_<name>_init(), which the same file declares and whose body makes only the calls of the protoc-gen-go registration (a file_<name>_init, len, reflect.TypeOf, PkgPath, unsafe.Slice, unsafe.StringData, the Build of the type builder and a conversion such as (*T)(nil)). Expects no package-level var, of any name, whose value calls a function that the generators do not write there (the listed calls of errors, regexp, the runtime's command, query and authz packages, the entity views of the generated data package, make and the helpers must, mustCommand, mustQuery and declare); a conversion to a parenthesized type or to a type that the file declares is no fault, and a parenthesized function such as (register)() is. In the body of file_<name>_init, PkgPath counts only on reflect.TypeOf and Build only on a protoimpl.TypeBuilder literal. Expects the second apply to write the same main.go. Expects the build to write one binary from the one main package out.
notes: Proved by TestServiceBindsItsDeclarationAtBuildTime, TestProtobufRegistrationIsTheOneAllowedInit and TestPackageStartCalls, subtests ST-GEN-INV14-T. Before this test, out/internal/storage/migrate.go registered the generated migrations in func init. The postgres-adapter (6.7.1) now registers them in registerGenerated, which orderedMigrations calls once. A mutation that puts the func init back fails the test. Decision on ST-GEN-Q42, reading a: ST-GEN-INV14 does not cover the descriptor registration of protoc-gen-go, which decides nothing that runs. The second test shows that only that exact pattern is allowed. The real path covers rest-crud. TestRuntimeWiring (internal/compiler) runs the binary of a rest-crud service against a database. The security review of #394 (L3) found that the check missed a var _ = f() at package level, which runs at start as a func init does, and trusted the header and the name of file_<name>_init without its body; both are now faults, with a case each. The security review of #401 (L1 to L3) found that a call in parentheses passed as a conversion, that Build and PkgPath passed on any value, and that a named var could run a call at start; each is now a fault, with a case each.

title: Planning and apply stop at a pin that does not stand unless it is overridden by name, and an unread lifecycle is not a pass
when: With a project in a temporary folder and its lifecycle records: planning and apply run with each pin standing; with a component digest superseded and its fail date ahead; with it past its fail date; with the runtime version past its fail date; with a withdrawn digest that the record already pins and its fail date ahead; with that withdrawn digest past its fail date; with a new pin to a withdrawn digest whose fail date is ahead; with the digest past its fail date overridden by name; with two pins past their fail dates, both overridden by name; with the same two pins and only one overridden; and with lifecycle records that cannot be read.
then: Expects the runs with standing pins, with a supersession whose fail date is ahead, and with the withdrawn digest already pinned and its fail date ahead to go on, the last one naming the digest as withdrawn with its fail date. Expects each run with a pin past its date, withdrawn past its date, or new to a withdrawn digest to stop, to name the pin, and to write nothing. Expects the run with the override to go on and the record to name the overridden pin and its reason. Expects the run with both pins overridden to go on and the record to name each of the two pins with its reason. Expects the run with one pin overridden to stop, to name the pin that is not overridden, and to write nothing. Expects the run with unreadable records to stop, to say that the standing could not be checked, and to name no pin as current.
notes: Decision of the Product owner on ST-DIS-Q01 of 2026-11-04: a pin to a withdrawn digest that the record already holds is refused only after the withdrawal's fail date, and a new pin to it at once (ST-DIS-UC07-R02, R03). The case of the withdrawn digest already pinned with its date ahead catches a check that refuses every withdrawn pin at once; the new pin case catches one that waits for the date for every pin. The standing is Distributing's (ST-DIS-QRY03); the test writes real lifecycle files. The fixture writes each lifecycle date relative to the day the test runs, so the test needs no clock seam.

title: The emitted failure record never formats its cause
when: Reports a stage failure whose cause panics when formatted, and the bare cause, into a buffer.
then: Expects the cause kept for errors.Is and errors.As, a five-field record with the fixed event, severity and message, the right stage, and an RFC 3339 timestamp; and a record of a failure with the selected modes to hold them as a sixth field, modes, with no error text.
notes: The subtest of TestGeneratedHTTPLifecycle that carries this ID runs, in the generated project, TestFailureRecordDoesNotFormatCause with TestFailureOutputHasDeadline, TestFailureOutputDoesNotRetry and TestFailureTaskNamesAreData of internal/compiler/testdata/service_failure_test.go, which assert the stage-name set and the bounded write, so the outcome is theirs. Each of the four tests of that file runs its checks in a subtest that carries this ID, as ST-STD-CODE-R04 asks of every test file (the gate note of #240). The test of the deadline waits 1.5 s for the record write to give up, so a deadline of 2 s fails it (#241 review); mutation caught: a deadline of 2 s.

title: The emitted supervisor waits for a canceled task
when: Cancels a running task that holds its return, then releases it; also starts the supervisor with an already canceled context.
then: Expects no return before the release, a nil result after it, and no task started after cancellation.
notes: The subtests of TestGeneratedBackgroundLifecycle that carry this ID run, in the generated project, TestCancellationWaits with TestCanceledStart, TestTaskSignal, TestParentCancellationBeforeChildPropagation and TestCancellationKeepsOtherErrors of internal/compiler/testdata/task_lifecycle_test.go, which assert signal handling and shutdown classification, so the outcome is theirs.

title: The emitted supervisor contains every kind of task abort
when: Runs a broken task that panics with a string, with nil, with an error whose formatter panics, in a deferred call, or calls Goexit, beside a peer that holds its return; the generated project runs this once more under GODEBUG=panicnil=1.
then: Expects the peer canceled only after the broken task's defers ran, no return before the peer's release, a failure without private text, and the broken task listed once as failed and once as aborted.
notes: The subtests of TestGeneratedBackgroundLifecycle that carry this ID run, in the generated project, TestAbnormalTaskExitStopsAndJoinsPeers and TestTaskFailureNamesExcludeCauses of internal/compiler/testdata/task_lifecycle_test.go, and TestAbnormalTaskExitStopsAndJoinsPeers once more under GODEBUG=panicnil=1, so the outcome is theirs.

title: The assembler checks task indexes and keeps task dependencies
when: Assembles with task indexes -1, 1 and 0,0, and computes the consumed constructors for a worker that depends on a store.
then: Expects each bad index refused and the worker's dependency chain consumed.
notes: Constructor resources are asserted by TestResourceArgumentsUseTheSelectedDatabase and TestInvalidConstructorResourcesFailAssembly in internal/compiler/resources_test.go; the index and middleware rules by TestConstructorMetadataIndexesMustExist and TestPrimaryMiddlewareSelectionMustBeUnambiguous in internal/compiler/constructor_metadata_test.go.

title: Every component's input check finishes before any component renders
when: With two components where the second refuses the declaration: run apply.
then: The first component renders nothing, and the run stops with the second's refusal.
notes: Known gap: wiring checks still run after rendering today (compiler-preflight-gap.md), so this invariant is partly false until they move.

title: A constructor dependency names exactly one producer
when: With two components that derive the same value name and a third that depends on it: assemble.
then: Assembly refuses and names the consumer, the dependency and both producers sorted.

title: The build target meets every active component's minimum Go version
when: With a component whose minimum is above the project's Go target: run apply.
then: Generation stops before any generator runs and names the component and both versions.
notes: TestPinnedDependenciesGateGoTarget in internal/compiler/dependency_target_test.go covers the dependency-driven minimum.

title: The input manifest is bounded, canonical and digested one way
when: With a manifest that holds 1025 files, an absolute path, a path under the output folder, or a serialised size over 4 MiB: save it.
then: Each is refused and nothing is written; the digest of a fixed manifest matches its vector.
notes: TestInputManifestRejectsMalformedState in the same file covers the other malformed manifests. TestInputManifestFillPresence shows that a version 2 manifest digests whether the project holds fills, and refuses a manifest whose fill presence does not suit its version.

title: A generated symbol never shadows a predeclared or startup name
when: With an import path ending in error and a constructor whose derived name would be NewError: assemble.
then: The import gets a distinct alias used everywhere, and the constructor name is refused before output.
notes: TestGeneratedImportsPreserveLanguageAndStartupNames and TestConstructorCannotShadowPredeclaredNames in the same file cover every predeclared and startup name, and TestAssemble_FillAliasConsistency in assembler_test.go the shared binding record.

title: A record is upgraded on the next run and decoded strictly
when: With a record that lacks the compiler build, then with one written by a different compiler build, then with one carrying an unknown field: run apply.
then: The first is completed, the second is a record change, the third is refused.
notes: TestStateFormatRejectsUnsupportedVersionsBeforeWrites in internal/compiler/state_format_test.go covers unsupported versions.

title: The assembler wires each declared mode as a named set in one binary that a repeatable mode flag selects
when: TestRuntimeWiring applies the test service, whose declaration states no modes, and its next release, which declares the modes controller, api and worker out of order, builds both binaries, and the check of testdata/runtime_wiring/check runs them against the local PostgreSQL server, SpiceDB container and Kafka broker: the binary with --mode bogus, the worker mode with no connection string of the worker role, the next binary with --mode all and with no mode option, each with no database setting; then the running service with no mode option, with --mode api, and with --mode api --mode worker. TestDeclaredModes reads the declared modes of the glue for no modes, [], an unordered list and a subset, and TestDeclaredModeVariable the allowed values of STEGO_MODE.
then: Expects the unknown mode refused at the stage modes before the database, the missing worker setting refused at the stage service.start.setting.postgres-adapter.STEGO_WORKER_DATABASE_URL with the modes [worker], and the next binary with --mode all and with no option to select api, worker and controller in that order, which its failure record names, each record with no error text and no value. Expects one binary: with no mode option the api set serves, the worker set connects as the worker role and the controller set holds the controller lease; with --mode api the api set serves, with no connection as the worker role and no holder of the lease; with --mode api --mode worker the api set serves and the worker set delivers the after slot of a create, with the lease free. Expects the glue to hold the declared modes in the order api, worker, controller, all three for no modes and for [], and STEGO_MODE to allow only the declared modes and all, so that stego env check refuses another.
notes: Proved by the check of testdata/runtime_wiring/check whose subtest carries this ID, which TestRuntimeWiring runs in CI with the local servers of the check (ST-STD-LOCAL), and by the subtests of TestDeclaredModes and TestDeclaredModeVariable. A service on the runtime data path must declare all three modes (ST-DECL-INV89), so a declared subset is not reachable in a binary today; the glue still refuses a mode the declaration does not state, as a second guard. The runtime registers the worker and controller sets on its mode registry in service.Start (ST-SUP-RP14-LC04). The constructor stages name their component, such as component.stego-runtime.constructor[0] (ST-GEN-INV16).

title: A run that emits a concern's code emits its check, and writes no record when a check fails
when: With four declarations, each with one concern only (tenant isolation, authorization, idempotency, ledger): apply runs for each; then apply runs for the tenant isolation declaration with a registry copy whose component breaks the isolation check.
then: Expects each of the four applies to write the check of its own concern as a generated file listed in the record. Expects the last apply to fail, to name the check that failed, and to leave the record and every file in the project as they were.
notes: One concern per declaration, so that a run that emits only some of the checks fails the test.

title: Conflicting HTTP routes of two components stop the run
when: ValidateHTTPRouteGroups reads route groups in which two components register the same pattern on the protected multiplexer, a public route conflicts with the protected fallback, and a pattern is not valid; then planning runs for two components that declare the same route.
then: It refuses each group and names the component, and it accepts groups whose protected and public routes do not conflict. The plan stops, names the route conflict, and writes no output, no module file and no record.
notes: The tests in internal/gen/http_routes_test.go cover registration failures and the protected mount.

title: Two applies at the same time give one writer and no mixed output
when: Two applies of the same plan start at the same time on one project; then a process that holds the lock dies.
then: Exactly one apply succeeds, the output shows no drift, and the lock is free after the holder dies.
notes: TestConcurrentApplyHasOneWriter and TestProjectLockIsReleasedWhenProcessDies each carry this ID in a subtest.

title: A binding to a slot no generator invokes is refused
when: With a registry component that declares a slot no registered generator consumes, and a declaration that binds a fill to that slot: validate it.
then: The check reports a slot fault that says no resolved generator consumes the slot.

title: A binding to a slot that no active component or bound mixin declares is refused
when: With a declaration that binds a policy fill to a slot no component declares: validate it.
then: The check reports a slot fault that names the unknown slot.

title: A setting of a component outside the active set, or one its schema refuses, stops checking and generation
when: With a component that declares one string setting: validate and plan declarations that set an unknown key, a value of the wrong type, a setting of a component that is not active, and a setting that is not a map.
then: Each check reports a fault, and each plan stops with a config fault before any generator runs.

title: An undeclared change to a base entity is refused, and a declared one that moves one phase is accepted
when: The check runs in process with the declaration and the record of ST-GEN-TD01 as base and these heads: User.email renamed to contact_email with no schema change; the same with the rename user-email-rename and its expand step; a new entity Team with no schema change; the same with an add change for Team; base steps in another order; a base schema change removed from head; from a base with no step, a head that gives user-email-rename its expand and its contract step; a searched field of a listed entity marked pii, a list taken away, an upsert key changed, and a list taken away under a rename; a new order of the fields of User; against a record that names components and no postgres-adapter, the same new order and a list taken away; and, from a base with no tenancy, with a record that names postgres-adapter only and with one that names no component, a head that adds pooled tenancy. Also, on the index check of the collections alone, which the check uses where generation cannot carry out the declaration: two renames of an implicit field of ActivityEntry (source_type to origin_type, then origin_type to kind_type) whose schema changes are listed in the other order than their steps; a searchable field nickname that an add step adds; a new implicit field action that the search of the list indexes already; display_name marked pii; and a list taken away. Also (TestBaseRelax) on User of ST-GEN-TD01: declared relaxes of a longer display_name, the new role owner, a default role, an optional email and role made a string; declared as relaxes a shorter display_name, a role taken away, metadata made required, role made a string of at most 20 characters, and a longer display_name that also changes its min_length; the same shorter display_name and metadata made required with no schema change; and four undeclared relaxes, each then with the relax that its fault declares. Also, on relaxRuntimeFaults, a new relax step on a base that pins postgres-adapter and a runtime library before v0.108.0 or none, at v0.108.0 and after, with no postgres-adapter, and a relax that the base has already. Also on User: a relax of the same max_length; two relaxes of role, its values and then role made a string; relaxDefinition of a default changed, a default taken away, a shorter max_length, a min_length changed and an enum made a string with a max_length; and CheckBase with a record that pins postgres-adapter 6.4.0 and the runtime library v0.107.0. Also (TestBaseDrop) on Organization and ActivityEntry of ST-GEN-TD01: a declared drop of the listed field Organization.description in its place; a drop of the entity ActivityEntry, kept with dropped_by; a drop whose Definition gives another place or leaves out the max_length; a drop whose Definition gives the field description the place first; an undeclared removal of description; and a removal of ActivityEntry and its collections with no dropped_by; a head that writes User.display_name, a searched field, sensitivity: public; and a base that writes it so, with the same head, over a record of postgres-adapter 6.17.0 and of 6.19.0. Then the unique step on bases whose record pins no runtime library, v0.182.0 and v0.108.0, and v0.183.0 and v0.190.0, a base with no postgres-adapter, the head as its own base, and a relax. Also (TestBaseRelateFaults, compiler.RelateFaults), from the user-management example and its schema as the base: the same head and schema; a head schema that gives organization the relation tenant of the subject type tenant with no relate step, and with the relate step organization-tenant-relate at expand; a head that binds no schema; a base whose schema has the relation already; and a base whose commit does not hold its schema. Also (TestBaseRelateFaults, security review of PR #495): a head that gives ActivityEntry a relationship owner from the caller, with no relate step, with the relate step activity-entry-owner-relate, and as its own base; a base with a shared entity Plan, and then the same with Plan system, and heads that give Plan a relationship owner from its field owner_id or the reference org_id with the relation organization, each also as its own base; and a base with no authorization setting against the user-management example with its schema, with no relate step and with the relate steps user-organization-relate and orgsetting-organization-relate. Also (security review of PR #497): a base with ActivityEntry#owner from the caller and a head with it from the field source_id, with no relate step and with activityentry-owner-relate; a base with owner from the field action and the same head; and a head that renames User.email to contact_email and adds the relation contact from contact_email.
then: Expects the heads with the declared rename and the declared add to be accepted, and each of the others to be refused with a fault that names ST-GEN-INV33 and the entity: the field marked pii and the changed indexes by what the generator gives for 001_initial of the base and of the head, the list taken away under a rename, which generation does not carry out yet, by the indexes that the collections describe, and the new order with one fault that names the table users of 001_initial. A permission changed, a new list or implicit field on a field that a search index has already, and a field that is not searched marked pii change no index and are accepted, and so is the new order against a base with no postgres-adapter, which has no 001_initial, while a list taken away there is refused by the indexes that the collections describe. The head that adds pooled tenancy is refused with a fault on 001_initial, because the baseline of each side is generated with the tenancy that its own settings select; no archetype or mixin of the registry names the tenancy component. On the index check alone: no fault for the two renames, the add and the new implicit field, and a fault for the field marked pii and for the list taken away (review of PR #263, L11). Expects the declared relaxes to be accepted, each narrowing to be refused with its reason and no relax to declare, each undeclared relax to give one fault that declares a relax with its definition, which the check then accepts; and the runtime rule to give one fault of ST-GEN-INV36 that names v0.108.0 and the change for each runtime before v0.108.0 and none otherwise (decision on finding F12 of the schema-change research, owner, 2026-11-13). Expects the same max_length to be refused, the two relaxes to be accepted, no relax from relaxDefinition for each of the five, and a fault that names v0.108.0 for the old runtime. Expects the drop of the field and of the entity to be accepted; the other place and the missing max_length to be refused through the baseline or the stored shape; the place first to be refused with a fault that names the column description out of place, after id in the head and after name in the base, and the definition to end with after name, and no CREATE TABLE text (walkthrough 20, W20-P-B); the undeclared removal to name the Definition with its place, after name; and the removal with no dropped_by to be refused, naming dropped_by; the field written public to keep its search index with no fault; and the base that writes it so to be refused over postgres-adapter 6.17.0 with a fault that names users_display_name_search and ST-DECL-Q46, and accepted over 6.19.0. Expects the three heads with the unique step to be accepted; unique: true with no step to be refused with one fault that names the unique step user-display-name-unique of User.display_name at expand, which makes the head pass when declared; the longer max_length to be refused; and a fault of ST-GEN-INV36 that names v0.183.0 and the change for each runtime before v0.183.0 or none, and no fault for the others (ST-GEN-Q48). Expects no relate fault for the same schema, the relate step, no head schema and a base with the relation; one fault of ST-GEN-INV33 for the new relation that names Organization and organization#tenant and suggests the relate step organization-tenant-relate with relation: tenant at expand; and an error for a base with no schema (core48 follow-up, decision ST-SUP-Q212 (a)). Expects one fault of ST-GEN-INV33 that names ActivityEntry, activity_entry#owner and the caller, suggests no schema change and tells the author to give the permission another path, also with the relate step, and no fault for the base with the relationship; one such fault for each new relation of Plan, shared and system, that names the field and the tenant kind, and no fault when the base writes it; and, for the base with no schema, one fault with a relate step for User.org_id and one for OrgSetting.org_id, which the relate steps clear (security review of PR #495, L1, L2, I1). Expects one fault of ActivityEntry.source_id with the relate step activityentry-owner-relate, which the relate step clears, and one fault of source_id when the base takes owner from action; and one fault of User.contact_email with a relate step for the new relation on the renamed field (security review of PR #497, L1, L2).
notes: The test calls compiler.CheckBase in process on two declarations as values and needs no git and no database. A base with the add steps of Team and User.nickname gives the cases of the base's step order and of a removed base change. A second subtest holds the bypass cases of the security review of #248: a change with no step to a field that a step of the base added, required or retyped, to a field of an added entity, to a unique invariant under its name, to an entity's table settings, and a new add of a unique field with a default; and it shows that the base itself and a new add after it are accepted (ST-GEN-Q11). Owner decision of 2026-11-06 (Q1): a removed schema change is refused, because the declaration keeps every change. Decision on ST-GEN-Q03 (owner, 2026-11-07): every change after the first release is a declared step, add included; stego apply writes the add step, and the check refuses a missing one. Review of PR #263 (L11): renames are traced in the order of the schema history, and the searchable fields of a listed entity count as indexed. Mutations caught (fu-71-mut.py): renames in list order; no searchable fields; the fields of an add step counted. One mutant is equivalent: searchable fields of an entity that no collection lists, because the description already holds the list flag. TestBaseRelaxLaterNoField shows that a relax and then a retype with no field are refused, naming the retype, with no stop of the check (security review of PR #372, M1). Mutation check: with the sensitivity before the seal not read, the two seal cases with a rename give the index fault. The unique cases of a field are subtests of TestBaseUniqueOfField with this ID in their names; the runtime gate of ST-GEN-INV36 is checked in process there, as the relax gate is. Mutations caught: no undo of the unique of a field; no suggestion of the unique step; no runtime gate. Mutation caught (fu/standing-43): RelateFaults gives no fault, so the new relation with no relate step passes. title: For each kind, v1 and v2 share one database and read each other's writes, and v2 and v3 do the same
when: From ST-GEN-TD04, each kind of v2's six schema changes is its own subtest with this ID in its name. The migration job of v2 runs; a v1 and a v2 replica each write a row that the change touches and read the other's row; v1 restarts. The backfills complete and the migration job of v3 runs; a v2 and a v3 replica each write a row and read the other's; v2 restarts; v1 starts. In one more subtest, on a copy of ST-GEN-TD04 with its own commits: w2 opens user-email-rename (A); w3 keeps A open and opens user-locale-require (B); w4 contracts A and keeps B open. The migration jobs of w2, w3 and w4 run in turn with the backfill of A complete before w4, and a w3 replica restarts after w4's migration.
then: Expects in each subtest every read to see the other release's write, v1 to restart and become ready after v2's migration, v2 to keep running during v3's migration and to restart and become ready after it, and the last start of v1 to fail with ErrMigrationLedger before it serves a request. notes: Not automated yet: schema steps are not built. notes: Not automated yet: schema steps are not built. title: Each setting selects its component, and a component that is not ga needs an acceptance

title: A changed body of a released migration is refused by compat, plan and apply, and the earlier body of a seal step that the head registers passes

In a second case, applies a seal of Note.body at expand and commits it as the base; then commits a record at the base whose digest of the expand step of the seal is an earlier digest that the generated migrate.go registers for it (the body of postgres-adapter 6.19.0 or 6.20.0, with the seal checkpoints in it), and runs stego compat, stego plan and stego apply; then gives the seal step at the base the digest of another body, with a migrate.go in the out folder that registers that digest by hand, and runs stego compat; then gives the seal step at the base the digest of another body, and 001_initial at the base the earlier digest of the seal step, and runs stego compat, stego plan and stego apply against each. In a third case, runs stego compat on the head as apply wrote it; then changes the generated migrate.go in the out folder by hand, gives the record of the head its new digest, and runs stego compat and stego compat --json; then runs stego compat with STEGO_REGISTRY set to a folder that does not exist, whose name holds a token.

In the second case, expects compat, plan and apply over the earlier digest of the seal step to pass with no fault of ST-GEN-INV38; compat with the hand-edited migrate.go to exit 1 with the fault that names the seal step; and compat, plan and apply over another body of the seal step, and over the earlier digest of the seal step given to 001_initial, each to refuse with the fault that names that migration, as an earlier digest counts only for its own migration. In the third case, expects no warning for the head as apply wrote it; then exit 0 and no fault, with a warning on standard error that names out/<path>/migrate.go, a new generation of the head, and stego plan --base HEAD as the gate of ST-GEN-INV38 (security review of PR #476, L1), and one JSON object with no fault on standard output; then exit 0 and a note that names the cause class registry or generation and holds no part of the error text, such as the token (security review of PR #482, L2).
notes: Each case runs the stego binary, as each test of ST-GEN-UC14 does. ST-SUP-Q170 (d). The second case is walkthrough 19, W19-U1: a service whose history holds a seal expand step that postgres-adapter 6.19.0 wrote could not upgrade, because #472 moved the seal checkpoints out of the body. Each case is a subtest with this ID in its name.

title: A head that keeps each event field of the base, or raises their version, is accepted, and each other head is refused
when: Checks heads against a base with a record whose Transaction declares Events of wallet_id, kind (enum) and amount at version 1: the same head; a head that adds the field note; a head without amount; a head with amount retyped by a schema change; a head with a value of kind removed; a head with no Events; a head with Events at version 0; and a head without amount at version 2.

notes: The test calls the base check directly, as the other tests of ST-GEN-QRY04 do. Decision ST-SUP-Q184 (c).

title: A local part with the name of a common part is refused, and a new local part is added

Then the local registry holds only local-a. Each time, the active registry is composed from the two sources.

Expects the composition with only local-a to give an active registry that holds every common part at its common digest, and local-a.
notes: A byte-identical copy is a replacement too, so a check that compares content in place of names fails the test. Each kind of part is a separate case, so a check that reads only components fails the test. The two sources are plain folders named as the common and the local registry; the system tests of ST-SUP-UC02-R01 compose the same refusals from pinned Git sources.

title: Every file a component plans is in its own namespace
when: With a test registry whose archetype holds stub-api (namespace internal/api) and stub-store (namespace internal/storage), plan the declaration and read the planned files. Then add the component bad-writer, with the namespace internal/bad, whose generator plans internal/storage/extra.go (in the namespace of stub-store), internal/bad-extra/x.go, ../outside.go, internal/bad/../storage/y.go and internal/bad/own.go, and plan again.

Expects the second plan to be refused, with no output folder written, and the refusal to name bad-writer, internal/storage/extra.go with the namespace internal/storage of stub-store, and each of the other three files as outside internal/bad, and not to name internal/bad/own.go.

title: A component below ga that provides the port of a ga component is refused
when: With ST-SUP-TD01, add the component beta-store (beta, a sunset date 30 days after today) that provides store-port, which the ga component store-a provides. Then add it at alpha. Then add it with the port beta-store-port, which no ga component provides. Then compose a registry in which a ga component and a beta component provide one port, once with each source first.

notes: Each case loads the registry, as stego registry compose does; the add of beta-store is a load of the registry that holds it. The compositions are two plain folders, one as the common and one as the local registry.

title: A mixin that replaces a part of its archetype is refused, and a mixin that only adds is accepted
when: With the parts of ST-SUP-TD01 that a mixin reads (svc-arch with api-a, store-a and auth-a, api-a offering before_create, svc-arch binding store-port to store-a, the second provider store-b, and twin and twin-b, which offer before_create and after_twin), load the registry with one more mixin that svc-arch names as compatible, one at a time: one that adds store-b, one that adds the slot before_create again, one that states overrides all, one that adds twin, one that adds twin-b and the slot after_twin itself, one that states a binding of store-port, and one that states a convention. Then load it with a mixin that names store-a, which svc-arch holds, and with svc-arch binding a port to extra-a, which only extra-mixin adds, and check extra-mixin against svc-arch. Then generate the slot files of an active set in which two components offer the slot check, ten times.
then: Expects each of the seven mixins to be refused, each refusal to name the mixin and the part it replaces (store-port, before_create, overrides, after_twin, bindings or conventions), and the first five to name svc-arch. Expects the mixin that names store-a, the binding to extra-a and extra-mixin to be accepted, and svc-arch with extra-mixin to hold the components of svc-arch and extra-a, and the one slot after_extra. Expects each generation of the slot files to be refused, naming the slot check and both components, and one component alone to be accepted.
notes: A mixin has no field for a binding or a convention, so the strict decoder refuses each by its path. A component the archetype already holds adds nothing, so a mixin may name it. The registry checks each compatible mixin of each archetype when it loads, and planning checks each bound mixin. The slot file refusal (internal/compiler/own_namespace_test.go) holds one contract for one slot name whatever the order of a map (sec-500 M1).

title: A provider that puts another meaning in a field of a port fails the port's conformance suite
when: With ST-SUP-TD01, add store-b, a second provider of store-port that fills the field version with a count that starts at 0 where the port means a count that starts at 1, and run the conformance suite of store-port against store-a and store-b. Then record the other pieces of the bar for store-b and try to graduate it to ga.
then: Expects store-a to pass the suite, and store-b to fail it, naming the field version. Expects the graduation of store-b to be refused, naming store-port and its suite.
notes: The suite is the mechanism by which providers are held to one meaning (see the notes of ST-SUP-UC09). The fixture provider differs only in the one field, so a suite that checks only the shape of the field fails the test. That a default provider must be ga is ST-SUP-UC09-R02, not this invariant.

title: A slot that no generator of its component invokes is refused
when: With ST-SUP-TD01, add api-a with a second slot after_create that its generator never calls but names in a comment; then with after_create called only by the generator of another component; then with after_create called by its own generator.
then: Expects the first two loads to be refused, each naming after_create and api-a, and the third to be accepted, with the emitted code of api-a calling the service of after_create.
notes: A slot named only in a comment or a string of the generator is not a call, so a check by text search fails the test.

title: A ga component without each piece of the quality bar at its current digest is shown below the bar and still loads, and its new version is not released as ga
when: With ST-SUP-TD01, read the quality standing of store-a after each change, one at a time: its security review removed, its benchmark removed, its design review removed, its reference comparison removed, one generator file changed so that its digest moves and all its evidence stays at the old digest, and one output contract changed so that the digest of its contract set moves. With the security review removed, also run stego registry quality and stego plan of the example declaration of svc-arch. Then release store-a at version 1.1.0 at ga with only the evidence of 1.0.0, and then with the four pieces recorded at the digest of 1.1.0.
then: Expects the standing of store-a after each removal to be below the bar, naming the removed piece. After the generator change, expects it to name the security review, the benchmark and the design review as made at the old digest, and not the reference comparison, because the digest of the contract set did not move. After the contract change, expects it to name the reference comparison as made at the old digest of the contract set. With the security review removed, expects stego registry quality to exit non-zero naming store-a, and stego plan to exit 0 with store-a still at stage ga. Expects the first release to be refused, naming 1.1.0 and each missing piece, and the second release to be accepted at ga.
notes: Decision on ST-SUP-Q04, reading b: a ga component below the bar is reported, not refused at load, because refusing at load breaks every service that pins it for a standing that moves. The plan case catches a load that refuses it. The reference comparison is held to the digest of the contract set, not to the component digest, so a check that holds all four pieces to the component digest fails the generator case.

title: An archetype pins one Go SDK by version and contents digest, and a build with another SDK is refused

Then, with the pin as it is, build the example service once with the pinned SDK and once with an SDK of the same version whose contents digest is different.

Then plan with the full stub-api, read the architecture model of the plan, change the code that the generator of stub-api emits and plan again.

Expects the model to place stub-api at its stated layer and flow part, with storage-adapter outbound and http-server inbound, and the second model to be byte-identical to the first.

Then add a component whose emitted code imports the runtime library at another version, and one whose emitted code imports another STEGO module. Then change the pin of svc-arch and keep its version.

Expects go.mod to require the runtime library at the pinned version, go.sum to hold the pinned checksum, and no other module under STEGO's module path to be required. Expects both components to be refused, naming the import. Expects the changed pin to be refused, naming svc-arch and its version, which must change.
notes: Proved by TestArchetypeRuntimePin; its subtest carries this ID. ST-SUP-TD01 is taken as one small registry in a temporary folder with svc-arch and one component hello, not as a Git commit: no pin check reads the commit. Two pins are two runtime keys, which the YAML decoder refuses as a duplicate key; the other four loads are refused by registry.checkRuntimePin. The example service comes from a stub generator of hello that emits a Go file that imports github.com/910-software-solutions/stego/registry/runtime/money. The import of github.com/910-software-solutions/stego/registry/runtime/v2/money is the runtime library at another version, and github.com/910-software-solutions/stego/other/money another STEGO module. The moved pin is refused against the archetype that the record (format version 3, ST-GEN-EN01) holds from the last apply, and a new archetype version moves it. Mutation check: the test fails when checkRuntimePin, runtimeImport or checkPinMove is taken out, or when the assembler leaves the pin out of go.mod or go.sum.

Then generate the example service with a fill for each slot of each shipped component, and list the Go types that the emitted code passes to each fill. Then run stego registry add on a fixture component whose slot code passes a *sql.DB to the fill, and on one whose slot code passes an http.ServeMux.
